question: When difference between compound and simple interest for three years is ₹183 at 5% interest per annum, the principal is ₹ ____________.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 3 years, CI and SI difference = P × (R/100)² × (300 + R)/100

183 = P × (5/100)² × (305/100)

183 = P × (1/400) × (61/20)

P = (183 × 8000) ÷ 61

P = 3 × 8000 = 24000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between CI and SI (D) = ₹183

Rate of interest (R) = 5% per annum

Time period (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Using the Tree Ratio Method for CI (refer to diagram):

Since R = 5% = 1/20, Let Principal be DenominatorTime = (20)³ = 8000 units.

 Total Difference = 20 + 40 + 1 = 61 units = ₹183

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for each year = 5% of 8000 = 400 units

⇒ Extra interest in 2nd year (CI on 1st year SI) = 5% of 400 = 20 units

⇒ Extra interest in 3rd year = CI on previous SIs + CI on previous extra

⇒ 3rd year extra = 5% of 800 + 5% of 20 = 40 + 1 = 41 units

⇒ Total difference = 20 + 41 = 61 units

⇒ Given difference = ₹183

⇒ 61 units = ₹183 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹3

⇒ Principal = 8000 units × 3 = ₹24000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tree Method Shortcut for 3 Years

For a fractional rate 1/x, if Principal = x³, the 3-year difference between CI and SI is exactly (3x + 1) units.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The direct formula for the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is D = P × (R/100)².

Effective Rate Method

Effective SI rate = 3R. Effective CI rate ≈ 3R + 3R²/100 + R³/10000. The difference is directly (3R²/100 + R³/10000)% of Principal.
